subject: Re: Follow-up: Model fit & multilingual evals for Aurelia Bank
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aureliabank.com>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@aureliabank.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: multilingual eval goals & next steps

Hi Liam / Sofia,

Thanks again for the call today - great to learn more about Aurelia's roadmap for localized customer messaging and onboarding flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

- Primary goals: 1) reduce translation/localization QA overhead for customer-facing flows, 2) ensure parity in tone and compliance across EU languages (FR/DE/ES) and select APAC locales (JA/KO).
- Key constraints: must stay within PCI/financial data controls (PII redaction), SLA for latency under 220ms p95 for synchronous UX, and a hard requirement to run custom evals before rollout.
- Immediate asks from Aurelia: sample prompt sets & benchmarks for FR/DE/ES + JA/KO, recommended model variants that balance cost vs quality, and a proposal for an eval plan that flags regressions on locale-specific prompts.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I will share a baseline prompt set and our initial multilingual benchmark (attached) for your team to run locally and we can iterate.
2) Internal pairing: loop in your ML lead if you'd like a joint eval session with our applied ML team (Neha/Rishi).
3) Schedule a 60-min follow-up demo + walkthrough of benchmark metrics (propose Wed 2026-03-04 10:00 CET) - let me know if that works.

Attachments: aurelia_prompt_set_v1.csv (sample prompts by flow & locale), rw_multilingual_benchmarks_20260301.pdf (baseline runs vs rw-multilingual-7b / rw-multilingual-13b).

If I missed anything from today's notes, flag it and I'll update.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aureliabank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@aureliabank.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: multilingual eval goals & next steps

Thanks Marissa - that captures it well. A couple clarifications from our side:

- For APAC we care most about Japanese (JA) first, then Korean (KO); Mandarin can come later.
- Our data team will need to validate that any sample prompts are scrubbed of account IDs; the attached prompt file should be fine but we'll confirm.
- Wed 03/04 10:00 CET works for Sofia and I. Please include Neha and Rishi from your side.

Can you also include a short note on expected cost delta between the 7B and 13B variants for the recommended batch sizes? That will help us model economics for the POC.

Best,
Liam
Senior PM, Customer Experience
Aurelia Bank
liam.oconnor@aureliabank.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aureliabank.com>
Cc: Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@aureliabank.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: multilingual eval goals & next steps

Perfect - looping Neha and Rishi on the technical plan. High-level recommendations up front:

- Recommended models: rw-multilingual-7b (cost-efficient baseline) and rw-multilingual-13b (higher-fidelity for nuanced tone/regulatory language). We can run a mixed routing policy during the POC: 80% 7b for throughput + 20% 13b for high-risk flows (disclosures, sensitive comms).
- Benchmark highlights (attached PDF): FR/ES show near-parity between 7b and 13b on intent accuracy, but DE and JA have larger deltas in stylistic fidelity and compliance phrase coverage.
- Eval approach: 1) run our baseline prompt set (attached) across both variants, 2) compute localization-specific metrics (BLEU + semantic similarity + hallucination rate on entity mentions), 3) set guardrails for automated regression alerts (we'll wire to your HubSpot eval tracker).

Cost note (very approximate for modeling):
- rw-multilingual-7b: ~0.8x baseline token cost (per-token inference), lower memory -> better batching.
- rw-multilingual-13b: ~2.2x token cost but significantly fewer style/regression failures in German/Japanese for our sample.

I've uploaded the prompt set + benchmark PDF to our shared Drive and added a lightweight bench viewer link: https://app.redwood.ai/benchmarks/rw-multilingual-2026-03-01
Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-multilingual-evals
HubSpot: HS-4821 (I've added a note under "Multilingual evals - POC").

Action items for Aurelia: please confirm a scrubbed sample of 300-500 prompts per locale (FR/DE/ES/JA/KO) so Neha can run the POC within our dedicated test pool. If you prefer, we can redact PII on our side - let me know.

Neha/Rishi - can you add any caveats on the DE/JA regression patterns you saw in the baseline runs?

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@aureliabank.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Sofia Martinez <sofia.martinez@aureliabank.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: multilingual eval goals & next steps

Quick technical notes:

- On DE/JA regressions: in our baseline runs the primary issues were (a) formal/informal register errors in German when prompts rely on polite forms (Sie/du), and (b) subtle punctuation and honorific handling in Japanese that affects entity linking. These show up as lower semantic-similarity scores and higher manual QA flags.
- Data handling: we can run the POC in a private test tenancy with KMS-backed keys; no customer data leaves the tenancy. If Aurelia wants us to redact on upload, we can do an automated pass that strips account IDs and hashes identifiable tokens.
- Eval pipeline: we'll produce per-locale dashboards (precision/recall-style metrics for intent + hallucination rate) and set automated regression thresholds that trigger a review. We recommend 3 checkpoint tests during the POC: smoke (initial), mid-POC, and pre-rollout (final).

I'll prepare a short runbook for the Wed walkthrough (will attach notebook + sample metric outputs).

-Neha
Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

See you Wednesday - looking forward to the walkthrough.
